finding: TWO HCP TASK RUNS WERE DOWNLOADED AND NEVER USED: EMOTION and RELATIONAL. Adding RELATIONAL is the largest in-fold gain found in the whole round.
how: task_merged.jsonl holds all seven HCP task FCs (971-972 of 972 subjects each); the chain only ever used five. Added them one at a time and together, on 728 subjects with all seven, 30 seeds, published folds.
verdict: RELATIONAL ADDS +0.0143 TO COGNITION, 30/30, t = 21.5 -- larger than every other in-fold lever found this round (motor drop +0.0034, keep-size freedom, alpha/w). EMOTION is actively harmful (-0.0051, 0/30). Seven together is +0.0110, i.e. useful but diluted by emotion.
the_emotion_target_is_untouched: the emotion-recognition deficit the ledger records is NOT helped by any of them: +0.0143 on cognition comes with -0.0029 on varimax_er. So this is not a fix for the deficit, it is a cognition gain from a task that happens to be about relational reasoning.
what_needs_checking_before_it_is_a_claim: (1) this is on OUR 400 extraction at g=0.85, not the published features at the headline setting; (2) it has been measured in-fold only -- every previous in-fold gain of this size (motor) failed out of sample; (3) the 728-subject subset with all seven tasks is not the 753 analysis set. The honest status is: a strong in-fold candidate that must be run on the published features and then on the 233 holdout before the paper uses it.
why_it_plausibly_works: RELATIONAL is the only HCP task that requires comparing two simultaneously presented stimuli, so its connectivity carries a comparison/reasoning signature that the other tasks do not -- and varimax_cog is loaded on reasoning. That is a mechanism consistent with the size of the effect, unlike a generic 'more modalities is better'.

fold_internal_verification_753.chosen_by_the_rule: (six modalities, g=0.85) 257/300, (six, g=0.92) 41, (five, 0.85) 2 -- the rule picks RELATIONAL in 298 of 300 folds

upgraded_verdict: RELATIONAL SURVIVES FOLD-INTERNAL SELECTION, which is the standard every other lever had to pass: with g and the modality set chosen inside the training fold, it gains +0.0134 (30/30, t=14.4) and the rule picks it in 298 of 300 folds. Fixed setting it is +0.0157 (30/30, t=19.6). This is the largest in-fold gain found in the whole round and the FIRST one whose mechanism (a comparison/reasoning task for a reasoning-loaded composite) matches its size.
still_required_before_the_paper: (1) the 233-subject holdout -- every previous in-fold gain of comparable size (motor) failed there; (2) the published Ooi features do not contain RELATIONAL, so the headline on published features cannot include it -- it must be reported as a result on our own extraction, or the published-feature arm re-extracted with the seventh task.
holdout_verdict: +0.0099 on 233 subjects never used in training, 95% CI [-0.0023, +0.0234], P = 0.94. This is the FIRST arm in the entire round whose in-fold gain survives the out-of-sample test with a positive point estimate -- the motor drop's +0.0034 did not, and neither did any extraction ensemble. The interval still includes zero, so the right wording is 'consistent with a real gain of about 0.01', not 'proven'.
status_final: RELATIONAL is now supported at three levels: in-fold fixed (+0.0157, 30/30), in-fold with g and the modality set chosen inside the fold (+0.0134, 30/30, and the rule picks it in 298/300 folds), and out-of-sample on 233 new subjects (+0.0099, P = 0.94). It is the strongest new finding of the round.
remaining_caveats: 1) the published Ooi features contain only five tasks, so the 0.7344 headline cannot include RELATIONAL; it is a result on our own extraction. 2) the holdout interval still crosses zero. 3) the holdout subjects are a subset of those with all seven tasks (232 of 263).
